issues.description: Field: Animal.name — The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the type of the Animal.name attribute. In the UML diagram (problem_statement.md) the Animal attribute is shown as 'name: String', while the textual instructions in the Part 1 section explicitly instruct students to use a StringBuilder for the name attribute to enable efficient in-place modifications. The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) uses a private field of type String. This inconsistency (UML: String vs. text: StringBuilder vs. solution: String) will confuse students about which type to implement and which getter/setter signatures are expected, and may cause test or compilation mismatches if tests expect one representation but students follow the other guidance.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification unambiguous: either (A) update the UML in problem_statement.md to show 'name: StringBuilder' and update example getter/setter signatures and any tests to use StringBuilder, or (B) change the textual instruction to require a plain String and remove the StringBuilder recommendation. Also update or add a short note explaining the rationale (performance vs. API simplicity) and adjust the reference solution and tests to match the chosen type. Finally, ensure the problem statement includes the exact expected getter/setter signatures (return and parameter types) so students know which type to implement.
